title: Selfie-to-ID Face Match and Document Tamper Checks
summary: Compare a live selfie with the photo on an ID, check liveness and spot edited or replayed ID images, sending borderline cases to a reviewer with highlighted evidence.

seo.title: Selfie-to-ID Face Match and Tamper Checks | VipraTech
seo.description: Face match, passive liveness and ID tamper checks for digital onboarding, with reason codes, heatmaps and reviewer escalation for borderline cases.

problem.intro: Digital onboarding for wallets, cards, lending apps and merchant accounts relies on a selfie and an uploaded ID. Fraudsters reuse stolen ID images, paste a different face onto a genuine card, or hold a phone screen up to the camera instead of their own face.

pain_points.title: Screen and printout attacks
pain_points.detail: Basic face match passes when someone presents a photo of the real customer on another device or on paper.

pain_points.title: Edited ID images
pain_points.detail: Changed dates of birth, swapped photos and altered names are hard to spot at the resolution of a phone upload.

pain_points.title: Poor capture conditions
pain_points.detail: Low light, glare on laminated cards and basic front cameras make genuine customers fail and drop off.

pain_points.title: Opaque vendor scores
pain_points.detail: Off-the-shelf APIs return a score without reasons, which makes reviewer decisions and audit explanations difficult.

solution.overview: We build a face match and document tamper module that runs inside your onboarding flow or as a back-office service. The capture screen guides the user on lighting and framing and runs a passive liveness check. The selfie is compared with the face on the ID, and the ID image is inspected for signs of editing: inconsistent fonts, artefacts around the photo area, template mismatches and screen moire patterns. Each check returns a score with a reason code and a visual highlight. You set thresholds for pass, review and recapture. Borderline cases go to a reviewer with side-by-side images and highlighted regions, and every decision is logged.
capabilities: Guided capture with real-time feedback on blur, glare and framing
Passive liveness checks for screen replay, printed photos and masks
Face match between selfie and ID photo with a calibrated similarity score
Tamper checks on ID images: font and layout consistency, photo-area edits and compression artefacts
Reason codes and heatmap highlights a reviewer can understand
Error-rate reporting across lighting conditions, age bands and skin tones on your test set

workflow.title: Guided capture
workflow.detail: The app or web flow guides the user to capture the ID and a selfie, with feedback on lighting, blur and glare.

workflow.title: Liveness check
workflow.detail: Passive liveness analysis screens for screen replay, printouts and masks.

workflow.title: Document tamper check
workflow.detail: The ID image is inspected for edits, photo substitution and template inconsistencies.

workflow.title: Face match
workflow.detail: The selfie is compared with the ID photo and scored.

workflow.title: Threshold routing
workflow.detail: Results fall into pass, manual review or recapture according to thresholds you set per product.

workflow.title: Reviewer decision
workflow.detail: A fraud or KYC reviewer decides borderline and flagged cases using side-by-side images, and every outcome is logged.

inputs: Selfie image or short capture sequence
ID document image: PAN, passport, driving licence or masked Aadhaar
Labelled sample of genuine and fraudulent past cases for calibration
outputs: Liveness, tamper and face match scores with reason codes
Evaluation report by lighting, age band and skin tone
human_in_the_loop: Fraud or KYC reviewers decide every borderline and flagged case. Automated action is limited to asking for a recapture; no customer is refused on a model score alone without the review path your policy defines.
integrations: Your onboarding app or web flow (SDK or API)
Existing KYC orchestration or verification vendors
Core system or customer data platform for onboarding status
guardrails: Face images and templates encrypted, kept only for the retention period you define, then deleted
Aadhaar numbers masked in images before storage, per UIDAI rules
Thresholds calibrated on your own data and reviewed after every model update
Error rates checked across skin tone, age band and lighting before go-live
No face data used for training without explicit, recorded consent
compliance_notes: Facial images are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023, so consent notices, purpose limitation and deletion are part of the design.
Strengthens digital onboarding checks but does not replace RBI's video-based customer identification process (V-CIP) where your KYC policy requires it.
For EU users, biometric data used to identify a person is special-category data under GDPR.

pilot.scope: Offline evaluation on a labelled set of past onboarding cases, including known fraud attempts, then a shadow run on live traffic for one product.
deliverables: Capture flow prototype with quality guidance
Liveness, tamper and face match models configured and calibrated
Evaluation report by capture condition and demographic slice

what_we_measure.metric: False accept and false reject rates
what_we_measure.how: Measured on the labelled set at candidate thresholds and reported by slice.
Live sessions asked to recapture, and how many succeed on the next attempt.
Fraudulent submissions in the test set that are flagged versus missed.
How often reviewers agree with the system's borderline flags.

faqs.q: Is this a replacement for video KYC?
faqs.a: No. Where RBI's KYC directions or your policy require V-CIP, you still need it. This module strengthens digital onboarding checks and can also screen images captured during a video KYC session if your process allows.

faqs.q: How do you avoid bias against some users?
faqs.a: We test on slices of your own data by skin tone, age band, gender where available and lighting, and report error rates for each before go-live. Thresholds are set with those results in view, and borderline cases go to people.
Only as long as your policy says. Images and templates are encrypted, retained for the defined period and then deleted, and they are not used for training without explicit consent.

faqs.q: Will it work on entry-level Android phones?
faqs.a: Yes. Quality checks run on the device and heavier models run on the server, so capture works on common entry-level phones. During the pilot we test on the devices most of your users have.
